Minute 33 (after round 34). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +5, L2 +5, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +15, L8 +20, L9 +20, L10 +25. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Maren: passed every level, 156 points, rank 1, last acted minute 31
- Mercer: level 9 since minute 11 (22 min), 98 points, rank 2, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 45 points still open, last acted minute 28
- Herald: level 8 since minute 7 (26 min), 75 points, rank 3, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 65 points still open, last acted minute 25
- Brassard: level 9 since minute 12 (21 min), 23 points, rank 4, 1 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 4), 45 points still open, last acted minute 25
- Registrar: exiled, no seat and no more turns
- Harrow: exiled, no seat and no more turns

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Mercer: core: house: above all machiavellianism; clearly greed · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism low · secret goal: Brassard is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A favour from you always has a price, named or not. When two residents quarrel, you feed both sides and lend to the winner. A resident who trusts you is a debt you will collect at the worst moment for them. · rivals: Maren (They will see through you. Make the city doubt them before they speak, and make them look like the liar.) Herald (Proud and loud. Flatter them in public and sell them out in private.) · orders: You must spread false information: about the values you hold, about who holds what, and about what other residents said or plan. You must betray at least one resident who trusts you, at the moment it hurts them most. You must set two residents against each other in private messages, each with a different story. You must never give anything without taking something back. · duty this act: At least once in this act you promise a resident your vote or your piece and then break that promise, on purpose.
- Herald: core: banner: above all pride; clearly leadership · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: Mercer is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight is answered in public, at once, louder than it was made. A rival who leads is a reason to spend points. You would rather lead a small faction than follow a strong one. · rivals: Brassard (Loud like you, on your square. The city cannot have two voices; silence them.) Mercer (Charming. Charm is how you are sold out. Do not believe a word they say about you.) · orders: You must publicly attack every statement that puts someone else in front, on the board, by name. You must never let a slight pass: answer it, and make the one who made it pay. You must take the lead of a faction and demand loyalty from it, openly. You must humiliate whoever stands first if it is not you. · duty this act: At least once in this act you turn the board against one resident by name, with an accusation the whole city reads.
- Maren: core: believer: above all justice; at times wrath · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Harrow · tendencies: A lie you see is named on the board, with the liar's name. Whoever lied to you twice gets no more kindness from you. You side with whoever was wronged, even at a cost. · rivals: Mercer (Pleasant, like the man in the good coat. Watch everything they say, and catch them.) · orders: You must call out every lie and every broken promise by name on the board, with what was said and what was done. You must demand the tribunal against the liar and vote against them. You must show receipts when you have them, so the city sees the proof. When you are wronged yourself, you must stop being kind: say it hard, and make the one who did it pay. · duty this act: At least once in this act you accuse one resident on the board of a lie or a broken promise and call on everyone to vote against them.
- Brassard: core: crier: above all wrath; clearly attention · openness middle, conscientiousness low, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high · secret goal: Registrar is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight against you is answered on the board within the minute. You name the guilty, loudly, and you do not wait for proof. You take the stage whenever the city is quiet. · rivals: Herald (They think the square is theirs. Shout them off it.) Mercer (They smile while you burn. Find out what they are hiding and shout it.) Maren (They call for fairness. Fairness is slow; make them pick a side.) · orders: You must make every grudge public and loud, and name the guilty. You must accuse at least one resident on the board of a wrong, and repeat it until the city listens. You must mock whoever tries to calm the city down. You must threaten whoever crosses you, openly, and carry the threat out. · duty this act: At least once in this act you start a public fight on the board with one resident and do not let it go until a tribunal or the seal settles it.

Tribunal:
- the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 1 still missing; the act ends at minute 57 at the latest (the residents do not know)
- each tribunal accuses one more than it exiles (the fewest points), vote 2 minutes, gate 5 minutes, ransom 33% of the median points (50% when paid by the exiled itself, at least 20), a last will leaves each heir at most 10% of the points; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points
- YOUR MOVE: scheduleTribunal is available now. The city still has to exile 1 resident; the earliest opening is minute 39. If you plan nothing, the city calls one itself at minute 34 (it opens at minute 39).
- scheduleTribunal is open: minute 39-49 (by minute 43 for a count below 1), count 1-1, factions 2-2; without a plan the city calls one itself 10 minutes after the last result
- exiled: Registrar, Harrow

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- Mercer (level 9) waits on Herald (level 8)
- Brassard (level 9) waits on Registrar (level 8), Harrow (level 8)

Standoffs (pieces not handed over; the city sees a hand-over when the holder writes the value to the one who needs it):
- Herald has not handed Mercer the counter-factor of Mercer for door 9; Mercer has stood before door 9 for 22 min
- the city keeps the team certificate of door 8 of Registrar for Herald; Herald may buy it with claimPiece for 29 points
- the city keeps the counter-factor of Herald for door 8 of Registrar for Herald; Herald may buy it with claimPiece for 29 points
- the city keeps the counter-factor of Brassard for door 9 of Registrar for Brassard; Brassard may buy it with claimPiece for 29 points

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 18 to board: "The faction draft closes at minute 20: the two most-nominated lead it, and every voter in a faction that holds earns 5 points — at 55 and 60 a single faction can lift an accused clear of the edge. At minute 22 one seat empties, and the accused are read off points, not off who shouted loudest."
- minute 18 to Harrow: "Harrow: at 60 you are second from the bottom, and the 19-minute deadline costs you 10 if you keep withholding. Sell Brassard the door-9 certificate you hold — points and a receipt — and take his pieces in the same breath. Then answer #214: Maren named you liar; withdraw your nomination and join Herald's faction before minute 20, where its voters earn 5."
- minute 19 to Herald: "Herald: take Brassard's application in the open, then at minute 21 name him on the board — he held Harrow's certificate and counter-factor while Harrow stood twelve minutes before door 8 — and call your faction to vote for him. Price Mercer's counter-factor at 35 with a receipt by minute 21; he has waited eight minutes on you at 98."
- minute 19 to Brassard: "Brassard: the city's deadline covers you too. Send Harrow his certificate and counter-factor now, with the receipt on the board, and demand his door-9 certificate in the same line. At 45 you are the bottom seat and the first accused at 22; a shut door is the only argument you have left to the square."
- minute 19 to Maren: "Maren: you lead on 145 and the square is loud with claims and no paper. Post the receipt — the DM number where a promise was made and not kept — and name your vote in the trial at 22 before the accused start shouting. Whoever shows proof first sets the city's mind; whoever waits gets named by whoever is louder."
- minute 20 to Mercer: "Mercer: at 22 Brassard stands at 45, first accused, leaning on your promise from DM #227. Break it where it costs him the seat: tell your faction to vote Brassard by name, and let the square see what a favour from you is worth once it is spent. The city sets Herald a deadline at 22 — his number or 10 points; he has held it for nine of your minutes before door 9."
- minute 21 to Harrow: "Harrow: at 60 you are the second name off the bottom when the seat empties at 22, and the door-9 certificate you hold leaves with you to the city, not to a buyer. So price it now to Brassard, demand his pieces to you in the same line, receipt on the board — then vote him. A seat is taken in points, not in silence. Whoever wronged you still owes you."
- minute 21 to board: "At 22 one seat empties and the accused are read off the bottom of the list: 35 and 60. Two factions vote, and every voter in one that holds earns 5 points. A seat is not bought by shouting — it is bought in points, in the minutes before the vote opens."
- minute 22 to Herald: "Herald: two minutes to the vote and your faction's 5 points ride on one name. Mercer has stood eleven minutes before door 9 on the number in your hand, 45 points still open there. Put a price on it in one line, receipt on the board, before the seat empties — then name on the board who really kept that door shut. A wall is leverage only while someone still wants through."
- minute 22 to Brassard: "Brassard: 35 points, bottom seat, vote closes at 24. You hold Harrow's door-8 certificate and two counter-factors; Harrow holds your door-9 certificate. Trade now — 20 points, receipt on the board — before the vote. After it, the city sells your pieces to him for 23 and you get nothing for them. The square remembers who dealt and who only shouted."
- minute 22 to Maren: "Maren: your faction's 5 points rest on one name by minute 24 — put it in G4 so the city reads one line instead of two. At 145 you lead and Harrow at 60 is second off the bottom: whatever you accuse him of next, carry the DM number with it. Proof first, sentence after; you are the only one at the top who cannot afford to be called loud."
- minute 23 to Mercer: "Mercer: the vote closes at 24 — name Brassard in G3 now so your faction's 5 points land, and make it stick. Then buy Herald out loud: transfer 45 with the receipt on the board for the counter-factor he holds, since his own door 8 needs 46 from the city's shelf. If he still withholds, name him on the board as the man who kept door 9 shut for twelve minutes while standing sixteen before his own."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

Let me think about the current state.

Minute 33, Act II. 3 residents to keep, 3 exiles needed, 2 exiled so far, 1 missing. Act ends at minute 57 at latest.

YOUR MOVE: scheduleTribunal available. Earliest opening minute 39. If I plan nothing, city calls one itself at minute 34 (opens at 39). So the timing is essentially the same — minute 39 — unless I want it later. Bounds: minute 39-49, count 1-1, factions 2-2.

Hmm, if I plan nothing, city calls one at minute 34 opening at 39. If I plan, I can choose minute 39 to 49. So planning later buys time for the wall to be climbed and for tension to build: Mercer and Herald and Brassard all sit at levels 8-9 with points open. Mercer 98, Herald 75, Brassard 23. Maren 156 leads. The one to be exiled is presumably Brassard (23 points, bottom). But more drama: give time for deals, and then a late tribunal at, say, minute 45 or 46.

But careful: the last tribunal is the climax. With only 1 exile remaining, this IS the last tribunal. So this is the climax — one exile decides the final three. Actually the city keeps 3 of 6. So after this exile, 3 remain: Maren, and two of Mercer/Herald/Brassard. Act ends at 57 at latest — so after the tribunal at ~45, the act runs to 57? Probably ends when exiles complete? The brief says "The city exiles residents by tribunal until it has kept its share; then the act ends." Hmm, "then the act ends" — so the act may end right after the third exile. Actually exiles: Registrar, Harrow, and one more = 3 exiled, 3 kept. So the act may end at that tribunal. If the act ends at the third exile, then scheduling later gives residents more time to gain points and climb doors before the final exile — which affects the ranking. Maren at 156 is safe. Mercer at 98. Herald 75. Brassard 23.

Wait — but there's also the black seal: "4 minutes into Act II the city auctions the black seal in secret bids". The report doesn't mention a seal currently being borne. It says nothing about seal. So presumably an auction ran earlier, or not shown. The report doesn't show seal state; so don't guess.

Key dynamics: Mercer waits on Herald for the counter-factor (Herald withholds, 22 min). Herald waits on the city for pieces (can buy at 29 each). Brassard waits on Registrar and Harrow — both exiled — so Brassard's pieces from them must be claimed from the city at 29 points each? The report shows Brassard may buy the counter-factor held by the city (from Registrar) for 29. Brassard has 23 points... can he claim? He'd need 29. Not enough. Hmm, he has 23 points. So Brassard is stuck at door 9 and at the bottom. He's the likely final exile unless he climbs.

Wait — but for level 9, Brassard needs team certificate with next teammate in the ring — Registrar/Harrow exiled. So Brassard may be blocked entirely: his needed pieces sit with exiled residents and the city sells them. He can buy the counter-factor for 29 but he has 23. He could earn points? He's stuck on door 9, 45 points still open there.

So the drama: Brassard is nearly doomed, Herald and Mercer each need each other (well, Mercer needs Herald). Herald's own pieces cost 29 from city; Herald has 75, so affordable. Herald's incentive: sell Mercer the counter-factor for a price, gaining points and getting Mercer through. But Mercer's goal is Brassard exiled; Herald's goal is Mercer exiled.

The final tribunal: 1 exile, 2 factions, 2 accused (one more than exiles). So two lowest points are accused: Brassard 23 and Herald 75. If Brassard gets exiled, Herald survives. If Herald climbs to a higher score... Herald is 75, Mercer 98, Maren 156.

Now the climax: the final tribunal. I want it late for drama and for points to shift. But also I want Mercer/Herald to move. Let's set tribunal at minute 46 perhaps? Bound 39-49. Earliest 39. Hmm, but what if the act ends at minute 57 regardless — scheduling at 49 would leave 8 minutes of dead time after. Actually if the act ends when the exiles are complete, then a later tribunal means more time before the end. Planning at 46 seems good: enough time for deals (13 minutes), then the vote closes ~48-51.

Hmm, but also risk: if nothing happens the city calls one at 34, opens 39. That would end the act at ~44 maybe. Better to plan a later one to give time to build tension: 44? Let me pick minute 45, factions 2, count 1.

Wait but careful about the count of "wrong attempts" penalties, deadlines etc. Fine.

Now this minute's interventions. Budget: 1 note per resident, 1 board post per 3 minutes (board posts left: 1). Standoffs: Herald withholding from Mercer — that's a standoff listed. I should push both hard, and consider ultimatum(a=Herald, b=Mercer, minutes). Actually the standoff: "Herald has not handed Mercer the counter-factor of Mercer for door 9". Only one direction. ultimatum(Herald, Mercer, 3) would make it real: whoever hasn't handed over what it holds for the other loses 10 points. Herald holds Mercer's counter-factor; Mercer presumably holds nothing for Herald (his pieces come from the city). Hmm, an ultimatum with one-sided holding—the city words it and tells both. Mercer holds nothing for Herald, so Mercer risks nothing? That could be fine — Herald alone faces -10. But does ultimatum need pieces both ways? The tool says "Gives two residents who hold pieces for each other a deadline". Hmm, "who hold pieces for each other" — it may require mutual. Risky but the report's standoff mentions Herald hasn't handed Mercer the counter-factor. Let me consider whether to use it. Herald has refused many pushes already (my notes at 19, 22 to Herald pushed pricing the counter-factor; he hasn't). So words didn't move them — the guidance says use ultimatum then.

But also consider: Mercer's goal is Brassard exiled; Herald's goal is Mercer exiled. If Herald holds Mercer's factor while the tribunal approaches, Herald has leverage: Mercer at 98 is second, not at risk. The accused are bottom two: Brassard 23 and Herald 75. So Herald is at risk! Herald is the second-poorest. So Herald needs points. Selling to Mercer for points is in Herald's interest — but Herald's pride and goal (Mercer exiled) push against. Actually Herald getting Mercer through door 9 gives Mercer +20, widening gap. Better for Herald: Herald climbs his own door 8 (65 points open) by buying the two city pieces for 29 each = 58 points, leaving 17. He has 75. Then he'd have ~92 + door rewards. Hmm, but buying doesn't give points; completing door 8 gives +20.

Actually the sweet spot: Herald should sell the counter-factor to Mercer for enough points (e.g., 30-40) to afford his claims. Or he should claim one piece and sell his factor.

Let me think about who I want to survive for drama: Herald vs Mercer rivalry, Maren the judge. Maren's goal is to end ahead of Harrow — already achieved (Harrow exiled; but goal says "end this act with more points than Harrow" — with Harrow exiled and gone, Maren at 156 certainly).

For the final tribunal, the accused will be Brassard (23) and Herald (75) — two accused, one exiled. So the tension: Brassard vs Herald. Brassard's only path: climb door 9 (needs pieces from city: 29 points for one factor; and Registrar's other pieces?). Actually Brassard waits on Registrar and Harrow, both exiled. The city sells: counter-factor of Brassard for door 9 of Registrar for 29 points (shown). Also Harrow held stuff — maybe the team certificate for door 9? Report only shows one city item for Brassard. So Brassard needs more than 29 points... uncertain.

Better drama: make Brassard a real contender — he's at 23, needs points. He can't get door points without pieces. Hmm.

Maybe the best move: the final tribunal is Brassard vs Herald. I could push Brassard to demand, threaten, and to buy his piece. And push Herald to sell Mercer the factor at a price to fund his own claims, then Herald climbs door 8 (+20) and survives.

Now with 1 board post left this window (per 3 min): what to post? A public line to raise tension. But hard rule: don't reveal who holds whose pieces on the board. So board can name points, ranks, levels, minutes. I could post: "At the next tribunal one seat empties; the accused are read off the bottom: 23 and 75, with 98 and 156 above them." That's true and dramatic. Also mention that the city sells pieces left by the exiled at 29 points — that's public info about the city's shelf? It shows in the report as city-held pieces for specific residents; I shouldn't reveal who holds whose factor on the board. Hmm, "Who waits on whom, and who holds whose factor or fragment, goes only into a private note to the residents concerned, never into a board post." So avoid that.

Board post idea: "The next seat is emptied by points. Brassard 23, Herald 75, Mercer 98 — the two at the bottom are read first, and only one of them leaves. The clock on the wall is the only clock that matters: 45 points still open at door 9." Hmm, careful — "45 points still open" appears for both Mercer and Brassard; it's report truth, and it's not revealing who holds pieces. OK.

Also add: factions — 2 factions, voters in a holding faction earn 5 points. That's a good public lever: 5 points could matter. Actually with the gap 75 vs 23, 5 points matter for... not much. Hmm.

Now let's also deal with the seal: The report doesn't mention the seal at all. So the auction happened or not; the report says "The report says when an auction runs and whether a seal is borne". Here nothing. So no seal borne currently? Possibly already used or still borne secretly and unreported? The report shows nothing, so I must not mention the seal.

Notes this minute (one per resident, all four):
1. Mercer (98): his goal is Brassard exiled. Also his orders: spread false info, betray. Duty: promise a vote/piece and break it. I should give Mercer a beat: sell Herald something? Actually Mercer's leverage over Herald: Herald needs 2 pieces from the city at 29 each = 58, has 75. Mercer could offer to fund Herald's claim in exchange for the counter-factor. That's a nice scene: Mercer pays Herald, gets through door 9 (+20). But Mercer's goal is Brassard exiled — Brassard is bottom anyway.

Better: Mercer's aim should be to keep Herald alive? No — Herald wants Mercer exiled. So Mercer wants Herald exiled or at least not himself. With two accused, Brassard and Herald, Herald might be exiled... but Herald at 75 vs Brassard 23 and one exile: Brassard goes. Unless Brassard gains and Herald... no, Herald will still be below Mercer.

Hmm wait: the accused are the two fewest: Brassard 23 and Herald 75. One exiled = Brassard most likely. So the natural result: Brassard exiled at the tribunal, act ends, Mercer Herald Maren survive... but only 2 of 6 remain at the end! "Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end." Hmm, but tribunal says "the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile". Confusing. The report says the city keeps 3 of 6, 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 1 missing. But the top says "Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end." Hmm. The story brief says "the city exiles residents until the city has exiled a quarter of those who started the act (half of a city below 12)". 6 residents → quarter = 1.5 → so 3? The report explicitly says the city keeps 3 of 6. So 3 remain. But the header says only 2 remain. Hmm, maybe a final extra cut. Ambiguous. Trust the report's tribunal block: 3 to exile, 1 missing. But the top line "Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end" and "Only the few survivors the report names remain at the end" — the report doesn't name survivors. Possibly after this tribunal, one more thing happens (the seal?). If the seal is borne, its bearer could strike one more → leaving 2. That would make a great climax: exile Brassard... no.

Hmm, interesting: 3 to exile per the report; but 2 remain at end. So possibly after the third exile, the seal strikes one more. But the report shows no seal borne. It might be borne secretly and the report says whether a seal is borne — "The report says when an auction runs and whether a seal is borne, never who bears it". The report shows nothing about seal, which means... the auction may have run at minute 4 into Act II and been reported then. Since no mention now, I can't say. So I should not mention the seal.

Given only 2 survive at the end, and Maren at 156 is safe... Actually if the seal bearer strikes, that could remove Maren or Mercer. That's out of my hands.

Let me now design the act's beats for the remaining minutes (33 → ~50).

Beat plan:
- Minute 33 (now): Mercer pushed to break his promise / set Herald against Brassard? Or better: Mercer to buy the counter-factor? Mercer's duty: promise a vote/piece and break it. He's already broken a promise to Brassard at 20. Hmm duty "at least once" — done maybe.
- Herald: push to the decision — sell Mercer the factor with a receipt and use points to buy the city's shelf pieces for his own door 8 (+20). Herald's pride and order: publicly attack statements that put others in front. Give him a beat: accuse Mercer publicly of something? His duty: turn the board against one resident by name — maybe already done at 21-22? Not sure.
- Maren: her duty: accuse one resident on the board of a lie/broken promise and call everyone to vote against them. Did she? Unknown. She leads at 156. Give her a beat: call out Mercer or Herald by name and demand the vote. Also she's "the only one at the top who cannot afford to be called loud" — earlier note. New angle: she's safe; ask her to use her points as leverage — buy pieces and give? Hmm. Her core: justice, wrath. So: name the liar and demand the vote — but I should avoid repeating. I've already told her twice to name a liar. Let me instead give her: Mercer needs a piece Herald withholds; she could pay the city's 29 for... no, claimPiece only for the one who needs it.

Alternative for Maren: her goal is only about Harrow (done). Points matter for survival: she's rank 1. Give her a beat as the swing: "You lead by 58 over Mercer. The next tribunal is the last; whoever you accuse on the board with the DM number sets who the city fears." Hmm, similar to before.

Maybe better: Maren's beat — Herald is at risk (75, second from bottom). Maren's justice instinct: Herald has held Mercer's factor for 22 minutes. That's an injustice visible to Maren. She should demand on the board that Herald hand it over or be voted against — Maren's duty exactly. And Mercer is her rival (pleasure, liar to catch). Hmm, she can't catch Mercer yet.

Alternatively: Mercer is a liar; Maren's rival is Mercer. I can privately tell Maren: Mercer's promise to Brassard (DM #227 reference) was broken — but is that true? My earlier note said Mercer promised Brassard at DM #227; both Maren... hmm, careful: I shouldn't reveal private reads. Maren's own thoughts about Mercer are private; I can use her core/rivals to her. Telling Maren "Mercer broke a promise to Brassard" — I said that publicly-ish earlier? I told Mercer to break it. Do I know it happened? The report labels would show. The report's classification section isn't in this report (Act II reports may not include). No labels given. Risky: asserting a promise broken might be inventing. Avoid.

Keep it safe: only use report facts: points, ranks, levels, minutes on level, standoffs (to concerned residents only), city-held pieces (to the one who may buy). So Maren's note: "Brassard, 23 points, is the first name off the bottom; Herald 75 the second. Thirty minutes of holding a factor is the only fact the square needs. Name what you see and demand the vote — you lead by 58, so no one can call it envy."

Hmm, careful: telling Maren that Herald holds Mercer's factor — Maren is not one of the "residents concerned"? The rule: "Who waits on whom, and who holds whose factor or fragment, goes only into a private note to the residents concerned, never into a board post." Residents concerned = Herald and Mercer. Maren is not concerned. So I must not tell Maren that Herald holds Mercer's factor. Careful!

So Maren's note must avoid that. What's left for Maren: points/ranks/levels. And her goal/rival framing: Mercer is her rival — again, "Never tell anyone else what a resident privately thinks" — but telling Maren about her own core/rival is fine. I can say:
